input.title: A chain link in another repo can tick its tracker box without routing its record there — #1691's CrosswordChat link blocks retrospective #1724
input.body:
Retrospective #1724 could not run. The reason is not the element it was filed to review — it is a gap in how a migration chain records a link that lives in another repository.

## What #1691 promised

The plan routes every link's result to the tracker: *"the plan routes every link's result there, which is what makes the chain's record readable from this repository."* #1724's "Read it from" column leans on that for **four of its six expectations** — which packs each member declared, whether the nine new checks fired on real member code, whether the `voice-on-a-host-page` fixture predicted the real adoption, and whether `host-page` gained a second adopter. Three of its four questions have no other source.

## What the record actually holds

#1691 carries exactly **two** comments:

| Comment | What it is |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-05T17:36:53Z (edited 2026-09-06T21:22:52Z) | the owner's phase tracker |
| 2026-09-06T21:22:24Z | **LaughCounter#394's** completion report |

CrosswordChat#396 never reported. #1691's body nonetheless ticks all five phases — including `- [x] **CrosswordChat** — CrosswordChat#396, now unblocked` — and #1691 was closed `completed` at 2026-09-06T21:23:12Z, **48 seconds** after the LaughCounter comment.

Note what the tick says: *"now unblocked"*, the same wording LaughCounter's row carries. The header of that same comment still reads "Three of five phases done". The boxes record that the links were *released*, not that they *landed*.

## Why the ticked box is not the record

A retrospective does not need to know that a phase finished — it needs what the phase found. LaughCounter's comment is the shape that works: which packs were declared, which checks were dropped for canon equivalents, which one was kept and why, the measured token counts, and the `dedup-prune-integrity` edge that any other member doing the same consolidation would hit. That last item is a lesson the fleet only has because the link wrote it down. For CrosswordChat, there is nothing.

## What cannot be distinguished from here

Whether CrosswordChat#396 **landed and did not report**, or **never landed and the tracker was closed early**. This session's GitHub scope is `missingbulb/Claudinite` alone, and `add_repo` is absent from its tool roster, so the link's own state is unreadable from this repository — which is the condition the local rule already names: *"a run here reads only this repository: its sessions carry no member's scope."*

Distinguishing the two is the first step on this issue, and it needs a session whose scope reaches CrosswordChat.

## Relationship to #409

#409 enforces that a tracker's checkbox is **flipped** in the same session as each merge that advances it. That invariant was satisfied here — the box is ticked — and the record is still missing, so #409 does not cover this. Its verifier design is also single-repo (`<!-- verify: <repo-path> -->` naming a script in this repo's tree); a link whose work lands in another repository has no such verifier to point at.

## Candidate remedies — none chosen here

- A chain link in another repository exits only when **its record is a comment on the tracker**, not when its box is ticked; the link's brief states that as its exit condition, as #1691's briefs already do for reading a dependency's artifact on `main`.
- The tracker does not close while any link's record is absent — the closing step reads for one comment per link rather than for a full set of ticks.
- A retrospective whose reads span repositories says so in its brief, and is either filed where those reads can be served or written to need only reads its own repo owns — which is the standing rule for verifications (*"Reproduce the premise on an object this repo owns, or file the verification on that repo"*) and is not yet stated for retrospectives.

## What was readable, and is clean

So that #1724 is not left wholly unanswered, everything its brief sources from this repository at HEAD:

| Expectation | Read | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Rules or checks reverted, softened, or moved to advisory — expected 0 | all 12 `worldRules` across `packs/host-page/`, `packs/web-speech/`, `packs/macos/` are `severity: 'blocking'`; no version cut on any of the three since `60904.1` (2026-09-04) | **0 — met** |
| Canon issues filed against the three packs — expected 0–2 | `search_issues` for `host-page`, `web-speech`, `macos`, `swift-toolchain-gate`: only #1692 (the promotion itself) and #363 (2026-07-19, six weeks prior) | **0 — met** |
| Implementation faithful to #1693 | `host-page` carries 11 rules and 3 checks with no `detect`/`marker`; `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` lists it `declared by hand (opt-in)`; `web-speech/worldRules/` holds exactly the six named checks; `macos/worldRules/` holds `swift-toolchain-gate` | **matches** |
| `voice-on-a-host-page` still green | the fixture stands at `vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs:1102`; the three packs' tests plus the rehearsal suite run **154/154 pass, exit 0** | **green** |

That covers "did the fixture stay green in the canon". It does **not** cover the half that matters more — whether the fixture predicted the *real* adoption, or whether a real member tripped a check the fixture called inert. That read is the one this issue blocks.

Questions 2 (misused), 3 (overused — findings waived or suppressed) and 4 (underused — `host-page` adopters) need member repositories and are unanswered for the same reason. The canon-side evidence is consistent with no waivers, but a member's own `accept` block is not visible from here.

Retrospective #1724 is parked `task:status:needs-human-action` naming this read, and left open. Clearing its status is what re-runs it, once the record it needs exists.

_Filed by the Claudinite task `claudinite-tasks/implement-request`, running as work item missingbulb/Claudinite#1724 — no person asked for this issue._

toolu_013dVaZ4Cm6FYNXebkwc9ACr.title: A chain link in another repo can tick its tracker box without routing its record there — #1691's CrosswordChat link blocks retrospective #1724
toolu_013dVaZ4Cm6FYNXebkwc9ACr.body:
Retrospective #1724 could not run. The reason is not the element it was filed to review — it is a gap in how a migration chain records a link that lives in another repository.

## What #1691 promised

The plan routes every link's result to the tracker: *"the plan routes every link's result there, which is what makes the chain's record readable from this repository."* #1724's "Read it from" column leans on that for **four of its six expectations** — which packs each member declared, whether the nine new checks fired on real member code, whether the `voice-on-a-host-page` fixture predicted the real adoption, and whether `host-page` gained a second adopter. Three of its four questions have no other source.

## What the record actually holds

#1691 carries exactly **two** comments:

| Comment | What it is |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-05T17:36:53Z (edited 2026-09-06T21:22:52Z) | the owner's phase tracker |
| 2026-09-06T21:22:24Z | **LaughCounter#394's** completion report |

CrosswordChat#396 never reported. #1691's body nonetheless ticks all five phases — including `- [x] **CrosswordChat** — CrosswordChat#396, now unblocked` — and #1691 was closed `completed` at 2026-09-06T21:23:12Z, **48 seconds** after the LaughCounter comment.

Note what the tick says: *"now unblocked"*, the same wording LaughCounter's row carries. The header of that same comment still reads "Three of five phases done". The boxes record that the links were *released*, not that they *landed*.

## Why the ticked box is not the record

A retrospective does not need to know that a phase finished — it needs what the phase found. LaughCounter's comment is the shape that works: which packs were declared, which checks were dropped for canon equivalents, which one was kept and why, the measured token counts, and the `dedup-prune-integrity` edge that any other member doing the same consolidation would hit. That last item is a lesson the fleet only has because the link wrote it down. For CrosswordChat, there is nothing.

## What cannot be distinguished from here

Whether CrosswordChat#396 **landed and did not report**, or **never landed and the tracker was closed early**. This session's GitHub scope is `missingbulb/Claudinite` alone, and `add_repo` is absent from its tool roster, so the link's own state is unreadable from this repository — which is the condition the local rule already names: *"a run here reads only this repository: its sessions carry no member's scope."*

Distinguishing the two is the first step on this issue, and it needs a session whose scope reaches CrosswordChat.

## Relationship to #409

#409 enforces that a tracker's checkbox is **flipped** in the same session as each merge that advances it. That invariant was satisfied here — the box is ticked — and the record is still missing, so #409 does not cover this. Its verifier design is also single-repo (`<!-- verify: <repo-path> -->` naming a script in this repo's tree); a link whose work lands in another repository has no such verifier to point at.

## Candidate remedies — none chosen here

- A chain link in another repository exits only when **its record is a comment on the tracker**, not when its box is ticked; the link's brief states that as its exit condition, as #1691's briefs already do for reading a dependency's artifact on `main`.
- The tracker does not close while any link's record is absent — the closing step reads for one comment per link rather than for a full set of ticks.
- A retrospective whose reads span repositories says so in its brief, and is either filed where those reads can be served or written to need only reads its own repo owns — which is the standing rule for verifications (*"Reproduce the premise on an object this repo owns, or file the verification on that repo"*) and is not yet stated for retrospectives.

## What was readable, and is clean

So that #1724 is not left wholly unanswered, everything its brief sources from this repository at HEAD:

| Expectation | Read | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Rules or checks reverted, softened, or moved to advisory — expected 0 | all 12 `worldRules` across `packs/host-page/`, `packs/web-speech/`, `packs/macos/` are `severity: 'blocking'`; no version cut on any of the three since `60904.1` (2026-09-04) | **0 — met** |
| Canon issues filed against the three packs — expected 0–2 | `search_issues` for `host-page`, `web-speech`, `macos`, `swift-toolchain-gate`: only #1692 (the promotion itself) and #363 (2026-07-19, six weeks prior) | **0 — met** |
| Implementation faithful to #1693 | `host-page` carries 11 rules and 3 checks with no `detect`/`marker`; `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` lists it `declared by hand (opt-in)`; `web-speech/worldRules/` holds exactly the six named checks; `macos/worldRules/` holds `swift-toolchain-gate` | **matches** |
| `voice-on-a-host-page` still green | the fixture stands at `vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs:1102`; the three packs' tests plus the rehearsal suite run **154/154 pass, exit 0** | **green** |

That covers "did the fixture stay green in the canon". It does **not** cover the half that matters more — whether the fixture predicted the *real* adoption, or whether a real member tripped a check the fixture called inert. That read is the one this issue blocks.

Questions 2 (misused), 3 (overused — findings waived or suppressed) and 4 (underused — `host-page` adopters) need member repositories and are unanswered for the same reason. The canon-side evidence is consistent with no waivers, but a member's own `accept` block is not visible from here.

Retrospective #1724 is parked `task:status:needs-human-action` naming this read, and left open. Clearing its status is what re-runs it, once the record it needs exists.

## The four questions, aimed at this element

1. **Working?** Did both remaining links converge, and does every member now carry exactly one local pack? Did the rehearsal fixture `voice-on-a-host-page` stay green through the members actually adopting — i.e. did the fixture predict the real adoption, or did the real member trip a check the fixture said was inert?
2. **Misused?** Has any repo put product requirements or a rule that would hold elsewhere into a repo-named local pack since the consolidation? The consolidation made one pack per repo the norm, and the risk it creates is a single pack becoming a dumping ground for anything local.
3. **Overused?** Did the nine blocking checks produce findings that were waived, suppressed, or worked around rather than fixed? A blocking check whose findings are routinely waived has the wrong severity.
4. **Underused?** Does `host-page` have exactly one adopter and no prospect of a second? It was promoted on the argument that its rules hold for any userscript, automation layer or content script; one adopter forever would mean that argument was wrong and it should have stayed CrosswordChat's local pack.

## Decisions this may re-open

**Cheap to revisit from evidence:**
- The severity of the nine new checks — all `blocking`. Evidence that would change it: findings waived or suppressed rather than fixed.
- `host-page` having no `detect` fingerprint. It was declared opt-in because a content script, a `dispatchEvent` and a `MutationObserver` are equally the shapes of code running on its *own* page. Evidence that would change it: adopters saying they did not know it existed, or a fingerprint proposal that separates guest from host.
- The `edfringe-now` size. #612 recorded ~940 lines and 34 rules under three headings, three times the next-largest local pack. Evidence it was wrong: rules in it going unfollowed, or a session unable to route a lesson into it.

**Expensive — treat as load-bearing, not re-openable on a week's evidence:**
- That `web-speech` and `macos` were widened rather than given new canon packs beside them.
- The pack ids themselves, now referenced from member declarations.

## What would mean a decision was wrong

- **The promotion itself**: if neither adopter's checks ever fire and no third repo wants them, the three facets were repo-specific after all and the canon shelf grew for nothing.
- **The fixture over a migration record**: #1693 chose the rehearsal fixture on the finding that no member declared the three packs. If either adopter went red on adoption in a way the fixture had not predicted, the migration record was the right call and the fixture gave false comfort.
- **The consolidation**: if a repo has since re-split its pack, one-per-repo was the wrong shape for it.

## Playbook

Re-read #1691, #1693 and the three packs' `RULES.md` **before** reading the record, then diff the record against what they promise. Answer the four questions with counts and links, not impressions.

File one issue per systemic fault, and fix nothing here. An implementation fault (the element does not do what #1693 says) is an actionable task issue. A design fault (it does what was designed and the record shows the decision was wrong) is a discussion issue carrying the evidence and the alternative from the "Decisions this may re-open" table, parked for the owner. Then comment the summary on #1691 linking each finding, and close this as completed. Four clean answers are a result too — close with the summary saying so.

If a read fails — a scope wall, a link's record never reported to #1691 — park naming exactly which read failed. A blocked read answers "all clean" the same way a healthy element does.
